title: Three Nights and One Short Thermometer
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：wound　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 wound 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the nurse ① dressed the wound that no sufferer in the ward would have measured, and he said the dressing was the whole of the night. The ② wound, meaning the injury itself and not the thermometer, ran three nights and stayed unmeasured in the book; a wound, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ wound in that ward had the same short thermometer beside it, and the ④ wound at the far cupboard, meaning the dose they kept for the children to take and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A wound, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the nurse said the measuring is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the wound was the whole of the matter, meaning the pain and not the injury. The ⑥ wound, meaning the pain and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; wound, he said, is either something you dress or the only word that means both an injury and a pain. He said the pain is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ wound had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short thermometer. The ⑧ wound of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in April, was one ward and three nights of measuring; wound, he said, is either the dose at the far cupboard or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ wound I remember is the injury measured in the report, which closed in 1970 and is still measured as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ wound, my mother said in 1972, is the only injury that improves by being measured; every wound, she said, is a pain that has agreed to look like an injury. She said the pain was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 伤口（指病房里每一处旁边的那一处）
B. n. 伤口（指那处伤口本身，与细细的体温计相对）
C. 固定搭配：dress the wound 包扎这一处伤口
D. n. 伤口（指留给孩子们服的那一剂）
E. n. 伤口之事（抽象总称，指一处病房的伤口之事）
F. n. 伤口（指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一处）
G. n. 伤口、隐痛（指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 隐痛（抽象总称，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: dressed the wound that no sufferer in the ward would have measured
The wound, meaning the injury itself and not the thermometer
the wound at the far cupboard
the wound was the whole of the matter
the wound had become a line in a report
The wound of the whole thing
A wound, my mother said in 1972

answers.why: dress the wound 意为“包扎这一处伤口”，1963 年那位护士把病房里没有一位病患肯测量的一处伤口做了一遍。
wound 意为“伤口”，指那处伤口本身而不是细细的体温计，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被测量。
wound 意为“伤口”，指病房里每一处旁边的那一处，每一处旁边都有同一支细细的体温计。
wound 意为“伤口”，指最远那格药柜的留给孩子们服的那一剂，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
wound 意为“伤口、隐痛”，指一件事里人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这处隐痛就是那件事的全部。
wound 意为“隐痛”，指人人都熬却无人提起的那样东西而不是那处伤口，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
wound 意为“伤口”，指护理记录里写到、被测量的那一处，到 1968 年这一处成了护理记录里的一行。
wound 意为“伤口之事”，护士四月写道，整件事的伤口之事是一处病房和三个夜晚的测量。
wound 意为“伤口”，我记得的是护理记录里测量过的那一处，1970 年挺过了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一处。
wound 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，伤口是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的伤口。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1963 年那位护士包扎了病房里没有一位病患肯测量的一处伤口，他说这一遍才是那个夜晚的全部。（dress the wound）
那处伤口，指的是那处伤口本身而不是细细的体温计，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被测量。（wound）
那处病房里每一处伤口旁边都有同一支细细的体温计。（wound）
最远那格药柜那处伤口，指的是他们留给孩子们服的那一剂，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（wound）
叔叔说这处隐痛就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那处伤口。（wound）
1972 年母亲说，伤口是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的伤口。（wound）
answers: In 1963 the nurse dressed the wound that no sufferer in the ward would have measured, and he said the dressing was the whole of the night.
The wound, meaning the injury itself and not the thermometer, ran three nights and stayed unmeasured in the book.
Every wound in that ward had the same short thermometer beside it.
The wound at the far cupboard, meaning the dose they kept for the children to take and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the wound was the whole of the matter, meaning the pain and not the injury.
A wound, my mother said in 1972, is the only injury that improves by being measured.
